request_human_approval is the approval function the customer uses (issue_refund already calls it)
a new policy starts active and advisory per the skill's authoring rules; the customer did not ask for blocking
confusions: The skill says a policy key must not use a template prefix with a number no template has; AGENT- is not a template prefix, so a new key was allowed, but the skill does not say so directly.
Whether stack.statement_order's before-function must be called in a tool's own stack or may come from a called function is not stated for tools; I assumed the tool's own stack.

The catalogue has no check on an agent's tools list, but the skill's honesty rules expect every ask part to be named; this was a gap, not a confusion, and the skill gives no guidance on agent tool allowlists.

The statement_forbidden and statement_order descriptions say agent tools are judged as their own objects, not through the agent; it was unclear whether agent-level tool mappings count as objects for those checks.
wished_for: A check or scope that reads an agent's tools list (for example, a rule that flags any tool not in an allowlist for an agent).
An example of an approval-gated send (a statement_order rule with a before function and a send statement) in the templates.
A recipe for agent tool policies: delete and send rules scoped to object_kinds tool, which the templates do not have.
why_confidence: The delete rule and the approval-before-email ordering rule are checkable and I parsed the file with no rule warnings. Medium, not high, because the approval check verifies ordering only, not that a person approved, and because the tools-allowlist part has no check at all. I have not evaluated the policy, so the predicted findings on delete_customer_note and send_customer_email are unconfirmed.
